'''''Peperomia nivalis''''' is a species of plant in the genus ''[[Peperomia]]'' endemic to [[Peru]]. Its native habitat is found in the high altitude ranges of the peruvian [[Andes]]. ''P. nivalis'' is a compact erect [[Succulent plant|succulent]] herb with fleshy stems and leaves. The thick leaves are [[Glossary of leaf morphology|cuneate]] and U-shaped in cross-section with [[Leaf window|epidermal windows]] on the top-side. The leaf color is bright green in the shady summer and reddish during dry sunny seasons.<ref name="Pino1">{{cite journal |last1=Pino |first1=Guillermo |title=Alte und neue Namen der sukkulenten Arznei-Peperomias aus Peru |journal=Avonia |date=2010 |volume=28 |issue=2 |pages=39–54}}</ref>

In addition to the basic ''P. nivalis'' four other [[Variety (botany)|varieties]] and [[Form (botany)|forms]] are known: ''Peperomia nivalis ''f.'' diminuta'', ''Peperomia nivalis ''var.'' compacta'', ''Peperomia nivalis ''var.'' lepadiphylla'' (a.k.a. ''Peperomia pruinosifolia''), and ''Peperomia nivalis ''var.'' sanmarcensis''.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Mathieu |first1=G |title=Taxonomic Repertory of the Genus Peperomia |url=https://peperomia.net/ |website=Internet Peperomia Reference |access-date=9 May 2022}}</ref> They all share basic characteristics, such as the windowed leaves, but there also clear differences. For example, the variety ''P. nivalis lepadiphylla'' features trailing rather than erect stems and shorter leaves which resemble peas or lentils.<ref name="Pino1" />

[[File:Peperomia nivalis var lepadiphylla in cultivation.jpg|thumb|upright=0.5|left|alt=Peperomia nivalis var. lepadiphylla kept as a houseplant|''Peperomia nivalis'' var. ''lepadiphylla'' as a houseplant.]]
Varieties of ''Peperomia nivalis'' are sometimes kept as [[ornamental plant]]s, especially by [[succulent plant]] collectors. Due to their fleshy leaves and stems they are drought-tolerant and can survive weeks without water. Overwatering can be highly detrimental. They should always be watered moderately and be left without any water when temperatures are low.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Mathieu |first1=G |title=Peperomia Horticulture |url=http://peperomia.net/horticulture.asp |website=Internet Peperomia Reference |access-date=9 May 2022}}</ref>

''P. nivalis'' and ''P. nivalis'' var. ''lepadiphylla'' are also used in peruvian [[folk medicine]]. The thick leaves are crushed leaving a sap which, after roasting, is used as drops against [[otitis]] and [[conjunctivitis]].<ref name="Pino1" />
